elements.label: Figure 2.12
elements.description:
Two-panel grouped bar chart (2010 vs 2020 series, teal and orange) comparing household income components.

Top panel, titled 'Annual household income (VND, million)'. Y-axis: 'Annual household income (VND, millions)', ticks 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150. Categories and approximate readings (no values printed; all approximate):
- Wage, bonus, severance: 2010 ~43; 2020 ~142
- Family business: 2010 ~47; 2020 ~144
- Family farms: 2010 ~29; 2020 ~33
- Remittance: 2010 ~7; 2020 ~14
- Social assistance (cash transfer only): 2010 ~5; 2020 ~10
- Pension: 2010 ~32; 2020 ~80
- Other income: 2010 ~3; 2020 ~5

Bottom panel, titled 'Share of household with income source (%)'. Y-axis: 'Share of households (%)', ticks 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. Categories and approximate readings:
- Wage, bonus, severance: 2010 ~65; 2020 ~71
- Family business: 2010 ~34; 2020 ~31
- Family farms: 2010 ~66; 2020 ~50
- Remittance: 2010 ~85; 2020 ~86
- Social assistance (cash transfer only): 2010 ~12; 2020 ~16
- Pension: 2010 ~8; 2020 ~9
- Other income: 2010 ~24; 2020 ~27

Notes printed below the figure: 'Nominal values. World Bank-constructed income categories. See Box 2.2 for definitions. Average incomes are only for households who report having the income source. Social assistance income includes only selected direct cash transfers.' Source: 'World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS 2010 and 2020.'

Pattern: average income from wages, family business and pensions rose sharply by 2020, while the share of households with family farm income fell, and remittances remained the most widely reported source.
